title: Your Lost Dog Can Now Call Home from Anywhere — Even the Middle of Nowhere!
summary:
Have you ever lost your dog on a hike and felt that panic when your phone says "no service"? A brand-new collar just solved that nightmare. It's the world's first dog tracker that talks directly to satellites, so your furry escape artist can be found even in the deepest forest or on a remote mountain.

The company Fi just launched the Fi Ultra Direct-to-Cell tracker on July 8. Unlike regular GPS collars that need cell towers, this one uses SpaceX's Starlink satellites. When your dog wanders outside a safe zone you set — like your backyard — the collar pings a satellite overhead. That satellite then sends your dog's exact location to an app on your phone. You can even set a virtual fence, called a geofence, so you get an alert the moment your dog crosses it.

The idea came from Fi's founder, Jonathan Bensamoun. He adopted a German shepherd named Thor and wanted to make sure his dog walker was actually taking long walks. But customers kept telling him the tracker was useless where cell service was spotty. When Starlink started connecting directly to smartphones in 2024, he knew he could fix that.

The collar also has a clever trick: you can send a gentle vibration or sound to your dog. If you train your pup to come home when they feel that buzz — maybe by giving a treat each time — they'll learn to race back even before you call them. The battery lasts multiple days, giving you plenty of time to find your runaway buddy.

About 11 million dogs worldwide already wear some kind of GPS tracker. But this is the first one that works almost everywhere on the planet. So next time your dog catches a deer scent and bolts, you can breathe a little easier.
why_it_matters: If you have a pet that likes to run off, this new collar could help your family find them faster, so you don’t have to worry as much during outdoor adventures.

background_read: Before this, pet trackers only worked where cell phone towers were nearby. In remote areas like forests or mountains, they were useless.
SpaceX launched Starlink satellites to offer internet from space, and in 2024 they started letting smartphones connect directly to them without special equipment.
Now, about 11 million dogs worldwide wear GPS trackers, but the new satellite-connected collar could help find pets in places where no cell service exists.

WHERE: Anywhere a dog might run away, even deep forests or remote mountains.
WHY: Because customers complained that GPS trackers were useless in areas with spotty cell coverage.

perspectives.description: They love that this collar can find a lost dog almost anywhere, giving them peace of mind even on remote hikes.
Some might worry that this high-tech collar will be too expensive, or that relying on satellites could mean a monthly fee.
They agree it’s a helpful tool, but remind owners that microchips, ID tags, and training are still important to keep dogs safe.
